Community Engaged Learning 
in Classrooms 
This year, the halls of People Incorporated's Early 
Education Center on Weaver Street in Fall River were 
transformed through the creativity and talent of 
UMass Dartmouth College of Visual & Performing 
Arts (CVPA) students. Made possible through the 
support of the Mass Cultural Council's Creative 
Experiences Grant Program, this collaborative 
project brought child-centered artwork into the 
Center's newest learning spaces. 
Children, families, and staff are now welcomed 
each day by three vibrant murals created by Class 
of 2027 students Madyson Trombly, Manuel Lewis, 
and Aleana Brayton. The project was completed 
under the mentorship of Jess Worby, a cartoonist, 
illustrator, art director, and Assistant Teaching 
Professor of Media Arts at the College of Visual & 
Performing Arts (CVPA). 
The murals celebrate imagination, exploration, and 
the joy of learning. A friendly giraffe greets visitors 
in the front lobby, sleeping bears create a calming 
atmosphere in the preschool wing, and a colorful 
tomato garden outside the kitchen encourages 
curiosity about nature and healthy foods. 
Opened in 2025, primary goal of the People 
Incorporated Early Education Center is to support 
families in promoting their child’s optimal 
development. The Center is a strength-based 
childcare program with goals that are family- 
centered, focusing on facilitating social interaction, 
exploration, and autonomy. The murals complement 
this vision by creating an environment that sparks 
wonder and supports children's development 
through engaging visual experiences. 
More than a collaboration, this initiative reflects the 
strength of community partnerships, the inspiration 
of art, and the importance of creating opportunities 
for youth to thrive.
